title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Purpose: This playbook centralizes canonical Redwood Inference go-to-market messaging for engineering and sales teams. It includes positioning statements, competitive briefs, a recommended pitch-deck narrative and slide checklist, pricing guidance and objection handling, representative anonymized case studies with measurable outcomes, and a short security FAQ for prospects evaluating hosted, dedicated, and private deployment options.

TL;DR Positioning (one-liners):
- Developer-focused inference platform: "Ship LLM features with predictable latency, unit cost, and operational controls."
- Multi-mode deployment: Hosted API (fast time-to-value), Dedicated (committed capacity), Private (regulated environments).
- Production-first economics: Batching, caching, quantization, and routing reduce unit cost while preserving quality.

Target personas: Platform/Infrastructure Lead, ML/Applied ML Lead, Product/Engineering Manager.

Core pillars:
- Reliability: multi-tier fallbacks, SLAs on Dedicated, per-route observability. Example talking point: "Keep chat endpoints within 150ms p95 at production scale using Redwood Dedicated."
- Cost predictability & optimization: Optimize tooling (batching, cache, quantization), per-token visibility, cost regression alerts. Example claim: "Typical customers see 20-40% unit cost reduction after 2 weeks of Optimize suggestions."
- Developer experience: REST/SDK onboarding, streaming, function/tool calling, consistent APIs across modes.
- Security & compliance: audit logging, KMS integration, private control plane, SOC2 evidence available.

Competitive framing (short):
- Public LLM APIs: highlight variability in cost and limited deployment control; Redwood offers reserved capacity and private deployments for predictable economics and residency.
- Self-hosted frameworks: emphasize operational lift and hidden engineering cost; Redwood provides runtime + orchestration + SLAs.
- Inference vendors: call out unified surface (hosted/dedicated/private) and developer UX.

Pitch deck narrative & checklist (Problem -> Why others fail -> Redwood -> Architecture/demo -> Pricing/TCO -> Case studies -> Security -> Next steps). Mandatory slides: Title, Customer pain, Value props, How it works, Deployment modes, Demo, Pricing & TCO, Case study deep dive, Security summary, Next steps/POC checklist. Appendix: model variants & quantization profiles for ML audiences.

Pricing guidance (conversation-level):
- Pillars: usage-based hosted (per-token/embedding), Dedicated (committed capacity monthly/annual), Private (platform fee + license/support + professional services).
- Sample (example only): Hosted: $0.0025 per 1K gen tokens; embeddings $0.010 per 1K units. Dedicated: monthly base + reduced per-token rate; 40-60% unit-cost reduction for steady workloads. Private: one-time platform fee + annual license.
- Discounting approvals: >20% list discount or multi-year concessions require ACV > $250k and Head of Revenue + Finance approval. Dedicated commits > $100k/month require Solutions Eng sizing.

POC playbook (3-week example):
Week 0: Discovery and success metrics.
Week 1: Trial setup (hosted sandbox or ephemeral Dedicated), baseline metrics.
Week 2: Optimization (prefix caching, batching, quantization), evals.
Week 3: Handover and TCO recommendation.
Success criteria example: p95 latency target met, >20% per-token cost improvement, no quality regression for top prompts.

Representative anonymized case studies (metrics summarized):
1) Conversational SaaS (Mid-market): p95 420ms -> 120ms; per-token cost -35%; 99.95% uptime.
2) Customer support automation (Enterprise, Regulated): Private on-prem + KMS; SOC2 readiness; AHT -22%.
3) Search & Reranking (Platform): embedding unit cost -48%; rerank latency 260ms -> 90ms.

Security FAQ (sale-ready):
- Where is data stored? Hosted: region-selected cloud storage; Dedicated: isolated in dedicated pool; Private: customer VPC/on-prem.
- KMS support? Yes, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) supported.
- Compliance evidence? SOC2 Type II reports, pen-test summaries available under NDA; compliance checklist for Private.
- RBAC & audit logs? OIDC/SCIM integrations, Console RBAC; audit logs capture token-level API access and admin ops.
- Preventing data leakage? Namespaced KV caches, logical tenancy, Dedicated/Private physical isolation; model-card reviews and guardrails.
- Incident response? Documented procedures and SLA-backed response for Dedicated/Private.
